newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - More selling reported.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - More selling reported.

text.p: Dealers in Oklahoma and Kansas said Thursday that sales of hard red winter wheat had increased Wednesday.

Dealers said Wednesday's rally in wheat futures may have played a role in triggering some selling by farmers. But dealers also said farmers' decisions to sell were not altogether related to price. Some need to generate cash ahead of Christmas and to pay fertilizer bills.
"We bought on the rallies and even continued to buy yesterday afternoon -- after the market had broken back," a south central Kansas dealer said.
Basis levels were steady to lower, reflecting the increase in sales.
Despite the lack of snow cover, dealers doubt the current cold will harm the winter wheat.
"No worries right now, at least," another Kansas dealer said. "It's a good crop, the ground's still pretty warm and the wind hasn't really been a factor yet."
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: H=KCBT March wheat futures. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
